source: Editing passes, scoring methods and style references harvested from primary sources (Editorial Freelancers Association, GOV.UK, digital.gov, W3C WCAG, NN/g, Google and Microsoft style guides, Mailchimp, IFCN, Hemingway, Yoast, UNC/Purdue writing centres) plus Wikipedia for named methods; URLs status-checked 2026-10-04.

items.name: Developmental edit
items.one_line: Big-picture pass on content, structure, argument and fit to the brief before any line work.

sources.title: Editorial Freelancers Association: Editorial service definitions
sources.supports: developmental editors deal with content, organisation and genre; deliver an edit letter

items.name: Line edit
items.one_line: Sentence- and paragraph-level pass on language, style, rhythm and clarity once structure is settled.

sources.title: Editorial Freelancers Association: Editorial service definitions
sources.supports: line editors work at sentence/paragraph level, focused on language and style

items.name: Copy edit
items.one_line: Correct spelling, grammar, usage, punctuation and consistency against a style guide; check cross-references.

sources.title: Editorial Freelancers Association: Editorial service definitions
sources.supports: copyediting covers spelling, grammar, usage, punctuation, cross-references and style sheets

items.name: Proofread
items.one_line: Final pass on the laid-out version for typos, formatting slips and changes that did not carry over.

sources.title: Editorial Freelancers Association: Editorial service definitions
sources.supports: proofreading is a late-stage check of the proof for typographical and formatting errors

sources.title: UNC Writing Center: Editing and proofreading
sources.supports: keep editing and proofreading separate; proofread with a plan for specific error types

items.note: Proofread after a break and on the final format (phone preview for social, rendered email) where possible.

items.name: Project style sheet
items.one_line: Keep a running list of the piece's or client's decisions (spellings, names, capitals, numbers, terms) and apply it everywhere.

sources.title: Editorial Freelancers Association: Editorial service definitions
sources.supports: copyeditors prepare style sheets that guide consistency

items.name: Reverse outline
items.one_line: After drafting, write one line per paragraph saying what it does, then fix order, gaps and repeats from that list.

sources.title: Purdue OWL: Reverse outlining
sources.supports: method for taking notes on and revising a draft

sources.title: George Mason University Writing Center: Reverse outlining

items.name: Cut-10% pass
items.one_line: Aim to cut about a tenth of the draft: needless words, repeated points, throat-clearing openers, weak adverbs.

sources.title: Anne R. Allen: Stephen King's 10% rule
sources.supports: describes King's formula from On Writing (secondary)

sources.title: Strunk, The Elements of Style (1920 ed., public domain)

items.note: The 10% formula comes from Stephen King, On Writing (2000), cited by name; it is a rule of thumb, not a measured target.

items.name: Verb and voice pass
items.one_line: Find passive constructions, hidden verbs (nominalisations) and weak verb + adverb pairs, and rewrite with strong active verbs.

sources.title: Yoast SEO: Readability analysis
sources.supports: passive-voice check; Yoast's threshold is 10% of sentences

items.note: Passive is right when the actor is unknown or unimportant; the pass is a review, not a ban.

items.name: Cliché and filler pass
items.one_line: Search for stock phrases, empty intensifiers and filler ('in order to', 'it is important to note') and replace or delete them.

items.name: Sentence-length audit
items.one_line: Flag sentences over the house limit and split them, while keeping some variety in length.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Use clear language
sources.supports: quote: 'Try to split up sentences that are over 25 words long.'

sources.title: Hemingway Editor: Readability
sources.supports: flags hard-to-read sentences; long sentences can still work for emphasis or rhythm

items.name: Jargon and word-choice audit
items.one_line: Replace jargon, buzzwords and internal terms with the words readers use; define unavoidable technical terms once.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Use clear language
sources.supports: plain English and words to avoid

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: Word list

items.name: Flesch Reading Ease
items.one_line: Score 0-100 from sentence length and syllables per word; higher is easier. English only.

sources.title: Flesch-Kincaid readability tests (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: formula and score table; 60-70 labelled 'Plain English. Easily understood by 13- to 15-year-old students.'

sources.title: Readable: Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level

items.note: Formula scores ignore meaning and order; use as a flag, not a pass mark. Yoast notes the Flesch score is English-only.

items.name: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level
items.one_line: Estimates the US school grade needed to read the text; pcw.py lint uses it as grade_max.

sources.title: Flesch-Kincaid readability tests (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: grade-level formula, developed with J. Peter Kincaid for the US Navy

sources.title: Hemingway Editor: Readability
sources.supports: Hemingway Editor Plus targets grade 9 by default, described as the US adult average

items.name: Hemingway Editor check
items.one_line: Run the draft through Hemingway to flag hard sentences, adverbs, passive voice and complex words, then fix the worst offenders.

sources.title: Hemingway Editor: Readability
sources.supports: what the highlights mean; scores are only a guide; default grade 9 target with accessible/technical options

items.name: Gunning fog index
items.one_line: Grade-level estimate from sentence length and share of complex (3+ syllable) words; another flag for dense prose.

items.name: Yoast readability analysis
items.one_line: WordPress plugin checks for passive voice, sentence length, subheading distribution, transition words and Flesch score.

sources.title: Yoast SEO: Readability analysis
sources.supports: list of checks and thresholds (passive voice 10% of sentences); Flesch and word complexity English-only

items.note: Tool thresholds are vendor choices, not standards.

items.name: Cloze test
items.one_line: Delete every Nth word, ask target readers to fill the gaps; their score measures real comprehension, not formula readability.

sources.title: NN/g: Cloze Test for Reading Comprehension
sources.supports: method; if users get 60% or more right the text is reasonably comprehensible for that audience

items.name: Reading-level check (WCAG 3.1.5)
items.one_line: If text needs more than lower-secondary reading ability, provide a simpler version or supplemental content.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 3.1.5 Reading Level (Level AAA)
sources.supports: threshold is the lower secondary education level, after removing proper names and titles

sources.title: NN/g: Lower-Literacy Users
sources.supports: lower-literacy readers plough text rather than scan it

items.name: Plain-language check
items.one_line: Review against a plain-language standard: reader identified, main point first, common words, short sentences, clear headings.

sources.title: digital.gov: Plain language guide (plainlanguage.gov redirects here)
ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language, Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines
sources.supports: international plain-language standard (page refused scripted fetch with 403)

sources.title: Plain Writing Act of 2010 (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: US law requiring plain writing in federal documents

items.name: GOV.UK style guide
items.one_line: UK government's public A-Z style guide and writing guidelines: plain English, frontloading, numerals, 'you'.

sources.title: GOV.UK A to Z style guide
GOV.UK writing guidelines
sources.supports: user needs, structure, clear language, tone, links, titles, summaries, change notes

items.note: Moved from gov.uk/guidance/content-design to guidance.publishing.service.gov.uk (old URLs redirect).

items.name: AP Stylebook
items.one_line: US news and PR house style for numbers, titles, dates, abbreviations and usage; the default for press releases and news copy.

items.name: Chicago Manual of Style
items.one_line: US book-publishing style for grammar, citation and manuscript preparation; default for books and long-form.

sources.title: The Chicago Manual of Style Online

items.name: Microsoft Writing Style Guide
items.one_line: Free tech-writing and UI style reference: warm, crisp, contractions, sentence case, bias-free, global English.

sources.title: Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Top 10 tips for Microsoft style and voice

items.name: Google developer documentation style guide
items.one_line: Free style reference for technical and product docs: voice, word list, headings, lists, link text, inclusive language.

items.name: Mailchimp Content Style Guide
items.one_line: Free brand-content style guide with voice-and-tone, grammar, accessibility and writing-about-people rules; a model for brand guides.

sources.title: Mailchimp: Voice and tone
sources.supports: voice stays constant, tone shifts with context

items.name: AI-tell removal
items.one_line: Find and rewrite the patterns that mark text as machine-written: inflated significance, promotional vocabulary, 'not X but Y', reflexive triplets, em-dash and bold overuse, chatbot residue.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing
sources.supports: field guide of patterns: undue emphasis on significance, promotional language, negative parallelisms, rule of three, boldface and em-dash overuse, communication intended for the user

items.note: pcw.py check applies a high-signal subset (AI_TELLS); the full method is the humanizer skill. Wikipedia's page warns that these are signs, not proof.

items.name: Fact-check
items.one_line: List every checkable claim (numbers, names, dates, quotes, causal claims) and confirm each against a primary source before publishing.

sources.title: IFCN Code of Principles: the commitments
sources.supports: same standard for every check; best available primary sources; transparent methodology and corrections

items.name: Source citation pass
items.one_line: Attach a named, linkable source to every statistic and quote, prefer primary sources, and date time-sensitive claims.

sources.title: IFCN Code of Principles: the commitments
sources.supports: provide sources in enough detail that readers can replicate the work

sources.title: Google Search Central: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
sources.supports: asks whether content presents information with clear sourcing and evidence

items.name: Plagiarism / originality check
items.one_line: Run the draft through a similarity checker and fix any unattributed overlap; quote and credit or rewrite.

sources.title: Content similarity detection (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: how plagiarism-detection software works and its limits

sources.title: UNC Writing Center: Plagiarism
sources.supports: what counts as plagiarism and how to avoid it

items.note: AI-content detectors are unreliable; never present a detector score as proof of authorship.

items.name: Grammar and spell-checker pass
items.one_line: Run a grammar/spelling checker set to the right language variety, then judge each suggestion rather than accepting all.

sources.title: LanguageTool
sources.supports: open-source multilingual grammar and style checker

items.note: Set en-IN / en-GB / en-US deliberately; checkers flag Hinglish and Indian English usages as errors.

items.name: Inclusive-language review
items.one_line: Remove biased, gendered, ableist or exclusionary wording and describe people the way they describe themselves.

sources.title: Google style guide: Write inclusive documentation
Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Bias-free communication

items.name: Sensitivity read
items.one_line: Have a reader from the depicted community review portrayals of identity, culture or experience for errors and harm.

items.name: Alt-text check
items.one_line: Confirm every informative image has alt text that conveys its purpose, decorative images have empty alt, and text-in-images is repeated in copy.

sources.title: W3C WAI: An alt Decision Tree
sources.supports: deciding alt text per image type

items.name: Link-text check
items.one_line: Make sure every link says where it goes on its own (no 'click here', 'read more' without context) and links are not overloaded.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
sources.supports: link purpose determinable from link text or context

sources.title: Google style guide: Cross-references and linking

items.name: Accessible writing check
items.one_line: Check headings are real headings in order, instructions do not rely on colour or position alone, and abbreviations are expanded.

sources.title: W3C WAI: Writing for Web Accessibility
sources.supports: writing tips: informative titles and headings, clear link text, alt text, simple language, expanded abbreviations

sources.title: Google style guide: Write accessible documentation

items.name: On-page SEO checklist
items.one_line: Before publishing: unique title and meta description, one clear main heading, descriptive headings, answer early, alt text, descriptive links and URL, no keyword stuffing.

sources.title: Google Search Central: SEO Starter Guide
sources.supports: baseline on-page practices and what not to bother with

sources.title: Google Search Central: Influencing your title links
Google Search Central: Control your snippets
Google Search Essentials: Spam policies
sources.supports: keyword stuffing and scaled content abuse are spam

items.note: Google states AI Overviews/AI Mode need no extra optimisation beyond these basics (developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features).

items.name: A/B test copy
items.one_line: Change one copy element, split traffic randomly, decide the success metric and sample size in advance, and keep the winner only if the difference holds.

sources.title: Mailchimp: About A/B tests
sources.supports: how email A/B tests on subject line, content, send time work

items.name: Headline testing
items.one_line: Write several headline or subject-line variants and test them on a slice of the audience before rolling out the winner.

sources.title: Nieman Lab (2023): what Upworthy's headline A/B tests showed
sources.supports: large analysis of real headline A/B tests

items.note: Headline families are hook: items; this is the testing method only.

items.name: Brand-voice audit
items.one_line: Score the draft against the brand's voice attributes and tone dimensions; fix lines that drift off-voice.

sources.title: NN/g: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice
Mailchimp: Voice and tone
sources.supports: worked example of a brand voice guide

sources.title: Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Brand voice

items.name: Content audit
items.one_line: Inventory existing pages or posts and judge each for accuracy, quality and performance: keep, update, merge or remove.

sources.title: NN/g: Content Audits
sources.supports: how to run a quantitative and qualitative content audit

items.name: Client feedback and revision rounds
items.one_line: Agree the number of revision rounds and what counts as a revision vs new scope up front; consolidate feedback into one list per round.

sources.title: Freelancers Union: Client issues
sources.supports: freelancer guidance on contracts and client problems

items.note: Low-confidence source; the round count is a contract term set per client, there is no standard number.

items.name: Pre-publish QA checklist
items.one_line: Final gate: facts and links checked, names and numbers re-verified, style and voice pass done, accessibility quick checks, preview on the target device, CTA works.

sources.title: W3C WAI: Easy Checks, a first review of web accessibility
sources.supports: quick accessibility checks (title, headings, alt text, contrast) before release

sources.title: Google Search Central: SEO Starter Guide
sources.supports: on-page basics to confirm before publishing

items.note: Composite checklist; the order and items are this harvest's synthesis of the passes above.
